text:
aaron: Quick idea: NUMA-aware coalesce + eviction hint propagation. We see a lot of PCIe blowback when coalesce moves/merges ranges that are then used by a vram-backed request on another GPU.

priya: Can you sketch the flow? sounds like we need affinity metadata on ranges.

aaron: Sketch: keep a preferred_node tag on free ranges updated by recent allocs. Coalesce prefers merging ranges with same preferred_node. When spiller picks victims, it emits evict_hints with target_node so allocator can try to expose ranges on that node first.

zheng: Hmm. How do we maintain preferred_node cheaply? Update on free fastpath with per-cpu stamp of last_alloc_node. But races with migrations/spills could make it stale.

aaron: It's heuristic, not strict. Use EWMA: preferred_node moves slowly. Also add last_touch_ts so coalesce can prefer recent-local ranges.

priya: What about cross-GPU batch reuse? If a batch migrates, preferred_node will lag and we might fragment. Maybe add a soft-migrate API that consumers call when they plan repeated access from a different node.

zheng: Soft-migrate could be a hint: consumer pins range with migrate_hint(node) and allocator tries to remap or copy if cheap. Need cost model: copy vs remote-read via PCIe.

aaron: Right. Add cost_estimate: copy_cost_ms vs remote_access_penalty. Coalesce should avoid creating large ranges that increase remote_access_penalty for noisy tenants.

priya: Telemetry: preferred_node_conflict_rate, coalesce_same_node_pct, remote_access_penalty_hist, migrate_hint_success. Console can surface hot-cross-node tenants.

infra-bot: nightly-sim scheduled numa-affinity-probe at 1887654330 :gear:

aaron: Edge cases: when preferred_node unknown, fall back to size-based coalesce; for Private customers expose knob prefer_local_coalesce=on|off. For Hosted keep conservative default.

zheng: Also consider NUMA-aware background scanner that nudges ranges towards local node when it sees long-run hotness on other node. But that is heavy. Start with hints-first.

priya: I'll prototype a model for migrate cost and a short RFC for preferred_node bits + hint API. If prototype shows >10% PCIe reduction in sim, we can try a small canary.

aaron: Thanks. I'll add minimal metrics to the PoC and attach sim results here.
